column2: Steeling myself, I stepped out into the raging blizzard.
Leaving the door wide open, I followed the trail of blood by the light spilling out from inside.
In slippers, it felt like my feet froze solid with every step.
After five or six steps the light lost its strength, and in the falling snow I could no longer follow the bloodstains.
I stopped and strained my eyes into the darkness.
In the dark, I saw two eyes glinting like a beast's.
The moment I thought so, a shadow, neither white nor black, came leaping at me out of the blizzard with a scream!
Before I could even raise the mop,
I was knocked flat on my back in the snow.
A terrible force clamped down on my neck and pushed my head down into the snow.
who is it!”
The moment I cried out through my crushed throat, the grip on my neck suddenly loosened, and I heard a startled voice.
{n1}, is that you?”
…It was Toshio's voice.
Hadn't he been
trying to kill me?
“Toshio…
is that you?”
The force pinning me down suddenly vanished,
and I heard a heavy thud.
Fearfully I sat up, and dimly saw Toshio lying in the snow.
His forehead was covered in blood, and his face was whiter than the snow.
Toshio, who might have butchered Mr. Kayama and the Kobayashis.
And now Toshio himself was badly hurt…?
I hesitated over whether to run, but in the end I stayed where I was.
“Toshio…
what…
what on earth happened?”
As if that freakish strength from before had burned him out, Toshio muttered in a voice about to fade away.
“It was him…
It really was him.”
“Him…?”
I asked, but my voice no longer seemed to reach his ears.
“I heard a strange noise, so I went out into the hallway…
and the door to the owner's room was open.
The moment I looked in, I got hit on the head.{r}{p}…He'd been hiding behind the door.{r}{p}I…
I ran for the back door as hard as I could.”
He seemed to be struggling to breathe.
“Who is he, Toshio?”
I crawled over to Toshio and shouted into his face.
“…I managed to get out the door and escape outside, but he locked it from the inside, and look at me now.{r}{p}…I…
…I'm done for.{r}{p}…Don't let him get you.{r}{p}…He's surely going to…
kill everyone…”
Toshio's voice faded out.
“Toshio! Who is it!
Who did this to you?”
I grabbed Toshio's shoulders, half buried in the snow, and shook him.
He might already be dead.
Even if he were still breathing, with no doctor around, there was no way to save him.
I dragged Toshio's body in through the back door.
Because I'd left the door open, snow had almost started piling up inside.
I dragged him to the relatively warm dining room and pressed my ear to his heart.
No matter where I listened, I couldn't feel a heartbeat.
Under the light, Toshio's face looked exactly like that of a dead man.
I was completely confused.
Toshio wasn't the culprit.
He said “he” had done it.
The Kobayashis too had been killed by the same “he.”
Who on earth was “he”?
Apart from {n2} and me, the only ones left alive were Haruko and the three office ladies.
They were all women, and none looked especially strong.
Were they supposed to have attacked the Kobayashis and beaten Toshio down as well?
Could it be Mr. Kayama….
Then I remembered I hadn't checked Mr. Kayama's pulse.
Neither {n2} nor I had touched his body.
Maybe he had only been playing dead?
And maybe he was still prowling around this building, waiting for his chance to kill us?
That can't be.
Mr. Kayama was definitely dead.
I felt I needed to confirm that Mr. Kayama was really dead.
Gripping the mop again, I slowly made my way through the dining room to the basement door.
The door was half open, exactly as it had been the last time I saw it.
I took a deep breath and started down the stairs.
Before I was halfway down, Mr. Kayama's body came into view.
He was lying at the foot of the stairs, just as when we'd found him.
Could that possibly have been playing dead?
After killing the Kobayashis and attacking Toshio, had he come back to the basement?
I descended the last few steps even more carefully, and first circled slowly around Mr. Kayama.
The choking smell I'd breathed so many times today showed clearly that the dark stain spreading out from beneath his head was blood.
I gently prodded Mr. Kayama's body with the end of the mop handle.
No reaction.
I knelt down and touched his wrist.
Cold.
I felt for a pulse, but again felt nothing.
Mr. Kayama really was dead….
My relief lasted only a moment.
Mr. Kayama really was dead.
Then what on earth was going on?
A zombie…
a living corpse… {g}
walking around and killing people when we weren't looking?
Otherwise I'd have no choice but to conclude that one of the women was a terrifying murderer….
……Wait a second.
A living corpse?
I knelt down quietly and, fighting back nausea, studied Mr. Kayama's face.
His eyes were wide open, and hair stiffened with blood clung to his split forehead.
I put my hand over his heart and felt for a beat.
Even through his clothes it was obvious he had no body heat, and I couldn't feel the faintest heartbeat.
I see…!
The pieces of the jigsaw puzzle clicked into place with a bang.
Now, at last, I knew who was behind this nightmare of a case.
It was….
It's me…{g}
No, enough joking around.{g}
I know better than anyone that I'm not the culprit.{g}
The culprit is….{g}
The culprit is Mikimoto….
Just as I became certain of it, a scream rang out from somewhere in the building.
No, it wasn't
{n2}'s voice.
I wanted to believe that.
I ran up the stairs to the first floor.
I could hear someone running down the hallway.
Another victim?
Damn it,
if only I'd noticed the truth a little sooner, just a little….
When I came up the stairs, I saw Mr. Kayama's wife, Haruko, collapsed on the floor.
I glanced quickly left and right, but there was no one else in sight.
“He” must have gone back to his room.
I crept up to Haruko on silent feet.
It was no use.
One look was enough to tell me she couldn't be saved.
A huge amount of blood had poured from her gaping forehead, and her hollow eyes no longer saw anything….
Now that I knew the culprit's identity, standing before the body, anger was far stronger than fear or sorrow.
Gripping the mop, I opened the door to Mr. Mikimoto's room.
On the bed, Mr. Mikimoto lay exactly as when I'd last seen him.
“Mr. Mikimoto,
you don't have to pretend to be a corpse anymore.”
I leaned against the closed door and spoke.
The “corpse” didn't move a muscle.
Had my deduction been wrong?
Just as I started to think so….
“…It was so close.{r}{p}Can't be helped now that you've seen through it.”
Mr. Mikimoto sat up with a groan and swung both legs off the bed.
“How did you know?”
“Your hands were too cold.{r}{p}Colder than Mr. Kayama's, and he was in a place colder than this.{r}{p}They felt like you'd been holding snow or ice the whole time.”
“…I see.
Guess I chilled them too much.”
Mr. Mikimoto clicked his tongue and pulled something out from under his clothes.
I tensed, thinking it might be a gun, but it seemed to be just a rolled-up towel.
“You used that to stop your pulse, didn't you?”
“…Yeah.{r}{p}That's right.”
If you clamp a ball or something under your armpit and press your arm down hard, you can stop the pulse at your wrist.
Of course, since it cuts off the circulation.
Anticipating that someone would come to check, Mr. Mikimoto had chilled his hands in the snow outside the window and waited with a rolled-up towel wedged under his arm.
I had faced far too many deaths.
As a result, I'd lost the capacity to verify each death properly.
And so I hadn't even been able to see through a trick this simple.
If I had seen through it at the start, Haruko wouldn't have had to die….
“Why did you do something so terrible?{r}{p}They were all…
all completely innocent people!”
I couldn't hold back my anger and shouted. Mikimoto… no, Mikimoto looked offended, as if I'd said something outrageous.
“No creature is as sinful as a human.{r}{p}We survive by taking countless lives.”
“That's…
that's just sophistry!{r}{p}Why did you kill them all?{r}{p}Mr. Kayama, the Kobayashis, Toshio, Midori…
and Mr. Tanaka, too!”
“Tanaka? {g}
I don't recall killing anyone like that.{r}{p}Well, in a sense you could say I did kill him, I suppose….”
I couldn't understand a word he was saying.
“But…
why did you come here alone?{r}{p}You practically walked in to get yourself killed.”
Mikimoto changed the subject.
There was no weapon in sight, but his expression was full of confidence.
“…Only girls are left.{r}{p}I couldn't let them get into danger.”
“Oh?
Playing the hero, are we?{r}{p}You'd better value your life.{r}{p}…Though it's probably too late for that.”
“Stay back!”
I hurriedly raised the mop.
Mikimoto, unfazed, slowly approached.
Pushed back by that eerie bloodlust, I stepped backward.
My back hit the door almost at once.
As I fumbled behind me for the knob, Mikimoto spoke mockingly.
“Running away?
Going to run and ask the girls for help?”
No good,
he could read me like a book.
As Mikimoto closed in, I screamed and lunged at him.
Mikimoto easily dodged the swinging mop.
And in the next instant, he was behind me, an arm wrapped around my neck.
In his hand, pulled out from who knows where, was a switchblade.
“Too bad.
It's over.”
The cold blade of the knife pressed against my throat.
The instant I heard that voice, there was a thud, and Mikimoto staggered.
Coming to my senses, I grabbed the knife hand with both hands and twisted free.
Mikimoto groaned and dropped the knife,
but immediately wrenched my arm behind me and slammed me down on the bed.
His hands closed around my neck and squeezed harder and harder.
“Ngh, ngh…
ngh…
gh…”
I couldn't breathe, and my windpipe hurt as if his fingers would break through it.
A white blankness opened up in my head and kept growing
wider.
Suddenly, the weight bearing down on me vanished.
Nausea and coughing rose up at the same time.
“Gagh, gagh…
cough!”
Opening my eyes a crack, I saw {n2} standing in the open doorway.
Staring blankly at her own blood-covered hands.
The moment she noticed my gaze, she snapped out of it and ran over.
…are you all right?”
I couldn't speak, so I nodded again and again.
“Thank goodness…
I…
I thought you'd been killed too….”
She clung to my neck and sobbed.
{n2} had stabbed Mikimoto to save my life.
I was ashamed that for even a moment I had found {n2} covered in blood creepy.
Without her, I would be dead.
And surely {n2}, and the office ladies too, everyone, would have been killed by this Mikimoto.
Mikimoto, lying on the floor, had stopped moving.
From the force of {n2}'s desperate charge, the knife was buried to the hilt in the middle of his back.
It's him.
It's me.
It must have reached his heart in one blow.
Compared to every murder he had committed so far, the amount of blood that flowed was astonishingly small.
As if there wasn't a normal person's worth of blood in his body.
But why had he had to do such terrible things?
And how had he killed Mr. Tanaka, who couldn't have been killed?
Now that he was dead, there was no one left to answer those questions.
But for now, {n2} and I could simply hold each other and wait for morning.
The long, long nightmare of a night was finally over….
“…So you're the culprit.”
For a while, Mr. Mikimoto didn't seem to realize I was talking about him.
“…Me?
You mean me? Stop joking around!
Ridiculous.”
{n2} chimed in too.
“That's right,
it can't be Mr. Mikimoto.{r}{p}He had no chance to kill Mr. Tanaka, and on top of that he's even got a head injury.”
“…Did you see how bad the injury is, {n2}?{r}{p}I didn't.
I only saw blood flowing.{r}{p}Mr. Kobayashi also said it didn't look like a serious wound.”
“Then…
then he was faking it…
no, you mean he only pretended to be hurt?”
“No,
of course he'd have cut himself with something.{r}{p}Maybe hit himself, or something like that.”
That was it.
It was the most convincing explanation.
This was a culprit who would go to the trouble of cutting up a body.
I couldn't imagine him half-heartedly hitting himself in a situation where he might be suspected.
So Toshio and Mr. Kobayashi, precisely because they looked suspicious, seemed less like the culprit.
Mr. Mikimoto laughed, looking half resigned.

“If you won't believe me, fine.{r}{p}But there's no way I could have killed this Tanaka person, no matter how hard I tried.{r}{p}Since I got here, I've been in this common room the whole time.{r}{p}…Except when I went to drop off my luggage
.{r}{p}So when exactly did I have time to kill someone and cut up the body?”
Everyone held their breath, waiting for my answer.
What if my idea was completely off the mark…?
The thought made me hesitate to speak.
I opened my heavy mouth.
“…You're right.{r}{p}You couldn't have killed Mr. Tanaka.{r}{p}You might have managed to kill him in the brief moment you went upstairs, but you couldn't have cut up the body.”
“See? I told you!”
I cut off Mr. Mikimoto's triumphant tone.
“Wait!
But the others didn't have the time either.{r}{p}We confirmed that earlier.
…Except for Toshio.{r}{p}…When we heard the glass break, Toshio was the only one who wasn't here.”
“Then he must be the culprit.”
“What did you say!?”
At Mr. Mikimoto's words, Toshio stepped toward him, openly furious.
“Now, now…”
I hurriedly calmed Toshio down.
“So for now, let's consider the glass incident as unrelated to the case.”
“Unrelated to the case?
Of course it's related! That's when the culprit escaped.{r}{p}It's obvious!”
Mr. Mikimoto waved a hand as if to say what nonsense I was talking.
“At first everyone thought so.{r}{p}Until Midori was killed.”
I continued.
“I went to Mr. Tanaka's room again earlier, and when I came out, the snow blown in from there left wet spots dotting the hallway.{r}{p}If the culprit had come back in from outside,
similar marks would have been left.{r}{p}Were there any such marks anywhere?”
I looked around, but no one answered.
“In other words, it's inconceivable that anyone came in from anywhere but the front door during this blizzard.{r}{p}Whoever killed Mr. Tanaka and whoever killed Midori must be someone here among us.”
“And how does that make it me?”
Mr. Mikimoto asked the obvious question.
I ignored that question and spoke to Mr. Kobayashi.
“Mr. Kobayashi.
When you found the body, didn't it look just like a doll?”
“Hm?
Oh, yeah.
It did look that way.{r}{p}But it was definitely a human, I tell you.”
Mr. Kobayashi stressed.
“That's right.
I think so too.{r}{p}But don't you think it looked like a doll because hardly any blood had flowed?{r}{p}And the body was bloodless, as if it were already half frozen.”
“Well, that's because the window was broken and snow was blowing in….{r}{p}But you're right, I don't remember seeing much blood.{r}{p}What's that supposed to mean?”

“At first I thought the culprit cut up the body in the bathroom or somewhere and then dumped it there.{r}{p}But the bathroom had no blood, not even a drop of water.{r}{p}So the culprit didn't cut him up in the bathroom.”
“What's that?
Then where'd they do it?”
Mr. Kayama cried out in a shrill voice.
“I get it!”
{n2} cried out.
“He was killed outside, right?
Killed and cut up outside, then thrown in through the window!”
I considered that possibility for a moment, but shook my head right away.
“No.
Hardly any of the broken glass fell inside, so that can't be it.”
“Not the bathroom, not outside.{r}{p}So where, exactly?”
Toshio said, irritated.
I looked into Mr. Mikimoto's eyes.
He seemed slightly shaken, which strengthened my resolve.
“Not the bathroom, not inside the room, not outside.{r}{p}Which means nobody killed Mr. Tanaka, and nobody could have cut him up.”
Silence lasted for a while.
Eventually Mr. Kobayashi began to laugh.
“What!?
So in the end, something like a kamaitachi attacked him?”
“No.
That's not it.{r}{p}What I'm saying is that the man called Tanaka was neither killed nor cut up.
…Isn't that right,
Mr. Tanaka?”
This time I could clearly read the shock in his expression.
Mr. Mikimoto was visibly shaken by my words.
The others all seemed shocked too.
“And here I wondered what you'd say…
ridiculous.{r}{p}I'm Yosuke Mikimoto.
I've even got a driver's license.”
“That beard is a fake, isn't it?{r}{p}It's coming off.”
Mr. Mikimoto put a hand to his chin as if startled,
and pulled it away immediately.
Then he grinned.
I never thought I'd fall for such a childish trick.”
“I didn't think it would work so well either.”
I grinned back.
“He's Tanaka?
What do you mean?{r}{p}Then who on earth is that body over there?!”
Mr. Kobayashi shouted in confusion.
“I don't know who it is, but it's definitely not Mr. Tanaka.{r}{p}That body was killed and cut up by Mr. Tanaka,
that is, by this Mr. Mikimoto.{r}{p}The body was probably cut up with its clothes on.{r}{p}There was suit fabric clinging to it, and even the sunglasses had fallen nearby.”
“They surely would have come off during the cutting, so I can only think the culprit deliberately left them there.”
“He left them there on purpose
to make us think it was Tanaka?”
“Surely.{r}{p}None of us knew Mr. Tanaka's real face.{r}{p}Without the suit and sunglasses, I think I'd have thought of this possibility much sooner.”
“…But where did that murdered person come in from?
And when was he killed?{r}{p}You just said no one came in.”
{n2} hit on the key point.
“Right.
I said no one came in except through the front door.{r}{p}Of course the victim came in through the front door too.{r}{p}Inside Mr. Tanaka's ski bag.”
“That's right.
The bag wasn't empty because something was stolen.{r}{p}What was inside was that body, already cut into pieces.{r}{p}The whole point of cutting up the body was to make it easier to carry.”
As I laid out the solution, I shuddered, picturing the horrifying scene.

“After dinner, Mr. Tanaka went back to his room, set that body by the window, rigged up a device, and then jumped out the window.{r}{p}Then he got into a car he'd hidden some distance away, drove a short way,
and called from some pay phone, pretending he was at the station.”
Everyone looked at Mr. Mikimoto.
No one doubted my words anymore.
“A device?”
{n2} asked.
“One that makes the window glass break automatically.”
“Break…
automatically?{r}{p}Is that even possible?”
“I think it is.
I don't know exactly how he did it, but I think it went something like this.”
I began slowly explaining the idea that had come to me earlier.
“Say the culprit goes out through one side of an outward-opening window.”
“The other side is fixed just enough that it won't move even if the wind pushes it.”
“Then he loosely hooks a rope, a meter or two long, onto the handle.”
“And to the other end of the rope he ties something flat, like a board…”
“Something like the bottom panel of a bag.”
{n2}: “So you connect the window and the board with the rope?{r}{p}What do you do with that?”
“Before jumping outside, he shoves the board into the snow piled on the roof.”
“Then after a while, the snow slides off, and the board falls with it.”
“The window gets yanked hard and slammed against the outer wall…
Crash!{r}{p}
And there you have it.”
“The board and rope come loose from the window and get buried under the snow.”

“I think Mr. Tanaka, that is, Mr. Mikimoto, had predicted it would happen around twelve.{r}{p}That's why he wrote that threatening letter and put it in Kanako's room.{r}{p}But he managed to make it in time to set up an alibi,
so there was no problem.”
“Why did he pretend to be attacked?”

“Because he didn't want anyone examining the area under that window, so he must have come up with that act out of necessity.{r}{p}On top of that, it let him steer suspicion toward Toshio, the only one without an alibi when the glass broke,
even further.”
Mr. Kobayashi said, staring at Mr. Mikimoto with wary eyes.
“…I understand how he did it.{r}{p}But why would he need to pull such a complicated stunt?{r}{p}Why did he have to bring the body here?{r}{p}Why my place?”
He sounded as if he wished it had been done somewhere else.
“Well…
you'd have to hear that from the man himself.”
I looked at Mr. Mikimoto.
The people sitting on the sofa all rose in fear and moved away from him.
Mr. Mikimoto gave a sheepish little laugh and yanked off his shaggy beard.
With the beard gone, his mountain-man look vanished without a trace, leaving only his cold-looking eyes standing out.
“Ahh, that itches.
Maybe the glue was bad.{r}{p}I'd been wanting to get it off.{r}{p}Mind if I go wash my face?”
Before I, standing between them, could stop him, Toshio lunged at Mr. Mikimoto.
“You…
You killed her!{r}{p}Did you really do it!{r}{p}…Answer me!”
Toshio pinned down Mr. Mikimoto, who was still seated, and began squeezing his throat.
In the instant I hesitated over whether to stop him, the situation reversed.
Before I knew it, Toshio was pinned face-down on the sofa with his arm twisted behind his back.
“Aah!”
Toshio groaned, perhaps from the pain.
“The rest of you, don't move either!{r}{p}I won't be responsible if his arm breaks.”
No one could move.
Mr. Kobayashi said, gasping.
“…Is it really…
really you…?”
Still holding Toshio down, Mr. Mikimoto nodded.
“Yeah, that's right.

I checked in under the name Ichiro Tanaka at first.{r}{p}A false name, of course.{r}{p}I copied that guy's handwriting for the signature in the guest register, so the police should never have doubted that he checked in himself.”
“Damn it!
Let go!”
Toshio shouted and thrashed.
Mr. Mikimoto twisted and shoved Toshio toward me.
Toshio fell onto me from the momentum.
{n2} lent a hand to help him up, and Toshio glared back at Mr. Mikimoto with burning eyes.
“That girl Midori, was she your girlfriend?{r}{p}It was a pity I had to kill her.{r}{p}Really.{r}{p}I've killed a few people so far, but only when I had no other choice.”
His matter-of-fact words sent a shiver through me.
This man was, so to speak, a professional.
A professional criminal.
As if confirming my thought, Mr. Mikimoto had produced an automatic pistol from somewhere and held it ready.
“Why…
why did you kill Midori?”
As I said it, I felt my mouth go dry.

“…She reached the same conclusion you did.{r}{p}More a woman's intuition than deduction, I'd say.{r}{p}I heard her say she'd examine the room with the body, so I waited until she was alone and went to see what she was up to,
and ran into her in the hallway.{r}{p}She said it straight out.
'You're Tanaka, aren't you?'
Just like that.{r}{p}There was no time to think things over.{r}{p}It was over in an instant, so she probably didn't have time to suffer.”
“Don't say whatever you please!”
Toshio said, and I felt exactly the same.
This man thought nothing of killing people.
To him, it seemed to mean no more than removing an obstacle.
Mr. Kobayashi repeated the question as if begging.
“Why?
Why did you do this?{r}{p}Why here?”
“Choosing this place was pure chance, of course.{r}{p}Anywhere would've done, as long as it was a remote inn where nobody who knew either of us would turn up.”
“Tanaka…
no, who was that body, really?{r}{p}Why did you kill him?”
I piled on questions too.
Mr. Mikimoto seemed willing to answer everything.
“He was my partner.
Though this job was the first and last we did together.”
“…A job?”
“Yeah.

The bank robbery.{r}{p}Your wild-guess deduction was actually right, you know.{r}{p}I planned the heist and set it all up; the one who did the actual job was that dead bastard, a small-time punk named Minami.”
Everyone looked astonished.
So was I.
To think that something I'd said on a whim had actually hit the mark….
“When you started saying that, I was sweating bullets over what would happen.{r}{p}I kept telling myself there was no connection to me.”
“Why did you kill him?”
“…From the start, we agreed to split it seventy-thirty.{r}{p}But the amount was bigger than expected, and that bastard got greedy and demanded half.{r}{p}He didn't seem very trustworthy anyway,
so I figured this was the time to get rid of him.”
“But…
you didn't need to go to such elaborate lengths.”
“Maybe not.{r}{p}But see, I mailed the money here in a box by courier.{r}{p}So it'd be safe even if I ran into a checkpoint.{r}{p}I had to come here one way or another.”
The money, by courier….
I was a little impressed.
“Making a body disappear completely is no easy job.{r}{p}And I'm on the run from the police, so I'm not free to move around.{r}{p}So I decided it was better not to try to hide the body clumsily.”
Mr. Mikimoto went on, boasting.

“He had a record; I don't.{r}{p}Once the body's identified, the police would figure he was killed in a falling-out among partners.{r}{p}I even left traces of someone escaping through the window.{r}{p}They'd comb the mountain, but they wouldn't suspect someone staying at the same inn,
and my alibi is airtight.{r}{p}No one could ever see through it…
was what I thought.”
His boastful tone finally dropped, and for a moment he lowered his eyes.
“But Midori saw through it, and you killed her.{r}{p}That ruined everything.”
I said accusingly.
“…Well, that's how it is.{r}{p}I still can't understand why she got suspicious, though.”
Mr. Mikimoto said, shaking his head.
Midori had probably doubted that Mr. Mikimoto had really been hit.
Unlike me, she was close to Toshio and Mr. Kobayashi.
So she must have believed they would never have hit Mr. Mikimoto.
And it didn't seem likely that the culprit was lurking around either.
Which meant that being hit had to be Mr. Mikimoto's own act.
But why would he do that…?
She must have built up her deductions like that.
Yes, right up until she brought about her own death….
“You might not believe me, but this is the first time I've killed an honest citizen.{r}{p}I do feel bad about it.”
He seemed to genuinely mean it.
“…So what are you going to do with us now?”
I summoned my courage and asked the question I'd been dreading.
“Relax.
Mass murder isn't my style.{r}{p}I'll think of another way.”
“Another…
way?{r}{p}What kind of way?”
“Oh,
nothing special.{r}{p}We wait for the money to arrive, then I leave. That's all.{r}{p}Naturally, you'll all tie each other up with rope.{r}{p}Otherwise I couldn't sleep easy.”
“Even tomorrow, with this snow, it might not arrive.”
When I said that, he hadn't thought of it, apparently, and his composure wavered.
But he quickly turned defiant and said:
“…If it doesn't arrive, I'll just wait until it does.{r}{p}Though I'm sorry for you folks.”
Then he raised his voice as if making a declaration to everyone.
“All right, confession time is over.{r}{p}Innkeeper,
you've got rope, right?{r}{p}Clothesline, anything will do.{r}{p}Go fetch some, will you?”
“Get it yourself.”
Mr. Kobayashi spat out.
“Don't make me say it twice.
You'll get hurt.”
He nudged the pistol to show it.
“Shoot if you want.”
Mr. Kobayashi, though pale, crossed his arms, leaning against the wall.
“What an uncooperative attitude.”
Mr. Mikimoto said, and swung the muzzle sideways toward Mr. Kobayashi's wife.
“Hey,
what are you doing!”
“…I don't recall saying you'd be the one who gets hurt.”
You scum.”
Toshio muttered, but no one seemed to hear.
“Fine!
Fine, just put that gun down.{r}{p}I'll go get it.”
Mr. Kobayashi hurriedly stood up.
